title: "19 — Train an AI/AN-only mental-distress model"
subtitle: "Run 0017 | Historical training, 2024 calibration, and paired 2025 comparison"
output: html_notebook

## Research question and rationale

**Would a logistic regression model trained exclusively on AI/AN-alone respondents predict frequent mental distress better for AI/AN adults than the nationally trained logistic regression model?**

This is a follow-up to the run 0017 subgroup evaluation. It uses the **same six predictor groups**, **same FMD outcome**, and **same processed feature definitions** as the main project. 

The notebook follows the existing calendar-year boundaries:

| Year | AI/AN-only analysis |
|---|---|
| 2014–2022 | Fit a new, AI/AN-only logistic model from the existing development checkpoint |
| 2023 | Examine raw probabilities on later AI/AN respondents; no model selection or tuning |
| 2024 | Fit a separate AI/AN-only probability calibrator |
| 2025 | Compare AI/AN-only and frozen national probabilities **on AI/AN-alone respondents** |

## 1. Attach to the existing project and run

```{r setup}
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) return(current)
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio before running this notebook.")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Use the same shared-module loader as the run 0017 notebooks.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing R chunk closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}

load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
check_packages(c("data.table", "ggplot2", "scales"))

run_context <- attach_run()
if (!identical(as.character(run_context$id), "0017")) {
    stop("This notebook is scoped to run 0017; attached run is ",
         run_context$id, ". Do not combine runs.")
}
if (length(primary_groups) != 2L || !identical(primary_groups[[1]], "AI/AN alone")) {
    stop("Unexpected primary_groups: check R/config.Rmd before proceeding.")
}

target_cohort <- primary_groups[[1]]
cat("[RUN]", run_context$id, "| AI/AN-only target:", target_cohort, "\n")
```

## 2. Load saved development, 2023, 2024, and 2025 datasets

The new model is fit **only** to AI/AN-alone records from the original 2014–2022 development checkpoint. This checkpoint already contains the harmonized variables and training weights used by the national models. Restricting it makes a like-for-like architecture and preprocessing comparison possible. The 2023 and 2024 records are not used to fit the base classifier; 2025 is not used for fitting or calibrating.

```{r load-and-audit-ai-an-data}
training_all <- data.table::as.data.table(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_development"))
selection_all <- data.table::as.data.table(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_selection_2023"))
calibration_all <- data.table::as.data.table(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_calibration_2024"))
scored_all <- data.table::as.data.table(load_run_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025"))
frozen_selection <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")

if (!identical(frozen_selection$chosen_family, "logistic")) {
    stop("The run's frozen national winner is not logistic. ",
         "This notebook requires a logistic-versus-logistic comparison.")
}

require_columns <- function(d, columns, stage) {
    missing <- setdiff(columns, names(d))
    if (length(missing)) stop(stage, " missing columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}

for (stage in c("training", "selection", "calibration", "2025")) {
    d <- switch(stage, training = training_all, selection = selection_all,
                calibration = calibration_all, `2025` = scored_all)
    required <- c("YEAR", "cohort", "AIAN_ALONE", "FMD", "RAW_WEIGHT", feature_names)
    if (stage == "training") required <- c(required, "train_weight")
    if (stage == "2025") required <- c(required, "source_row_id", "selected_probability")
    require_columns(d, required, stage)
}

# Match BOTH the saved cohort label and source-defined AIAN_ALONE flag.
# Subsetting with data.table's i expression keeps the saved feature encodings.
aian_train <- data.table::copy(training_all[
    cohort == target_cohort & AIAN_ALONE %in% TRUE &
    valid_outcome(FMD) & is.finite(train_weight) & train_weight > 0
])
aian_2023 <- data.table::copy(selection_all[
    cohort == target_cohort & AIAN_ALONE %in% TRUE &
    valid_outcome(FMD) & is.finite(RAW_WEIGHT) & RAW_WEIGHT > 0
])
aian_2024 <- data.table::copy(calibration_all[
    cohort == target_cohort & AIAN_ALONE %in% TRUE &
    valid_outcome(FMD) & is.finite(RAW_WEIGHT) & RAW_WEIGHT > 0
])
aian_2025 <- data.table::copy(scored_all[
    cohort == target_cohort & AIAN_ALONE %in% TRUE &
    valid_outcome(FMD) & is.finite(RAW_WEIGHT) & RAW_WEIGHT > 0 &
    is.finite(selected_probability) & selected_probability >= 0 &
    selected_probability <= 1
])

if (nrow(aian_train) < 1000L || nrow(aian_2023) < 100L ||
    nrow(aian_2024) < 100L || nrow(aian_2025) < 100L) {
    stop("Unexpectedly small AI/AN sample; verify cohort coding and checkpoints.")
}
if (!all(aian_train$YEAR %in% development_years) ||
    !all(aian_2023$YEAR == selection_year) ||
    !all(aian_2024$YEAR == calibration_year) ||
    !all(aian_2025$YEAR == 2025L)) {
    stop("Dataset year boundaries do not match the run configuration.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(aian_2025$source_row_id)) stop("Duplicate 2025 row identifiers")
for (d in list(aian_train, aian_2023, aian_2024, aian_2025)) {
    if (!all(d$FMD %in% c(0, 1)) || length(unique(d$FMD)) != 2L) {
        stop("Both binary FMD classes must be represented at every stage.")
    }
}

sample_audit <- data.table::data.table(
    stage = c("2014–2022: model training", "2023: raw diagnostic",
              "2024: calibration", "2025: paired evaluation"),
    n = c(nrow(aian_train), nrow(aian_2023), nrow(aian_2024), nrow(aian_2025)),
    actual_fmd_n = c(sum(aian_train$FMD == 1), sum(aian_2023$FMD == 1),
                     sum(aian_2024$FMD == 1), sum(aian_2025$FMD == 1))
)
save_table(sample_audit, "19_aian_only_sample_audit")
print(sample_audit)
cat("Predictor columns:", paste(feature_names, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 3. Train one new logistic regression using AI/AN-alone respondents

The frozen national model was chosen in the original project. Here we deliberately **hold the algorithm constant** and change the training population. A separate model output name prevents any change to the national model's checkpoints. No selection is made using 2025 outcomes.

```{r train-aian-only-logistic}
ai_model_path <- artifact_path("models", "19_aian_only_logistic", "rds")
if (file.exists(ai_model_path)) {
    cat("[REUSE] Previously saved run 0017 AI/AN-only model\n")
    aian_model <- load_run_rds("models", "19_aian_only_logistic")
} else {
    set.seed(seed + 1901L)
    aian_model <- fit_classifier("logistic", aian_train, NA_real_)
    save_once_rds(aian_model, "models", "19_aian_only_logistic")
    cat("[FIT] Trained and saved a new AI/AN-only logistic model\n")
}

ai_training_prevalence <- weighted_mean(aian_train$FMD, aian_train$train_weight)
cat("AI/AN-only historical training prevalence:",
    sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * ai_training_prevalence), "\n")
```

```{r raw-2023-comparison}

p2023_aian <- predict_classifier(aian_model, aian_2023)

    data.frame(model = "AI/AN-only logistic (raw)",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2023$FMD, p2023_aian, aian_2023$RAW_WEIGHT))
), fill = TRUE)
save_table(results_2023, "19_aian_only_2023_raw_comparison")
print(results_2023)

## 5. Calibrate the AI/AN-only model on 2024 AI/AN respondents

This uses the same procedure as Notebook 06, applied *only* to AI/AN-alone respondents. The classifier trained on 2014–2022 remains unchanged.

```{r calibrate-with-aian-2024}
calibration_model_path <- artifact_path("models", "19_aian_only_calibration_2024", "rds")
if (file.exists(calibration_model_path)) {
    cat("[REUSE] Existing run 0017 AI/AN-only calibrator\n")
    aian_calibrator <- load_run_rds("models", "19_aian_only_calibration_2024")
} else {
    raw_2024 <- predict_classifier(aian_model, aian_2024)
    log_odds_2024 <- stats::qlogis(pmin(1 - 1e-6, pmax(1e-6, raw_2024)))
    calibrate_data <- data.frame(
        outcome = aian_2024$FMD,
        score = log_odds_2024,
        model_weight = normalize_weights(aian_2024$RAW_WEIGHT)
    )
    cal_fit <- suppressWarnings(stats::glm(
        outcome ~ score,
        data = calibrate_data,
        family = stats::binomial(),
        weights = model_weight,
        control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 60)
    ))
    if (!isTRUE(cal_fit$converged) || any(!is.finite(stats::coef(cal_fit)))) {
        stop("The AI/AN-only 2024 calibrator did not converge.")
    }
    aian_calibrator <- list(
        intercept = as.numeric(stats::coef(cal_fit)[1]),
        slope = as.numeric(stats::coef(cal_fit)[2]),
        fitted_year = calibration_year,
        training_population = target_cohort,
        base_model_name = "19_aian_only_logistic"
    )
    save_once_rds(aian_calibrator, "models", "19_aian_only_calibration_2024")
    cat("[FIT] Saved AI/AN-only 2024 probability calibration\n")
}

raw_2024 <- predict_classifier(aian_model, aian_2024)
calibrated_2024 <- calibrate_probabilities(
    raw_2024, aian_calibrator$intercept, aian_calibrator$slope
)
calibration_audit <- data.table::rbindlist(list(
    data.frame(version = "Raw AI/AN-only model",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2024$FMD, raw_2024, aian_2024$RAW_WEIGHT)),
    data.frame(version = "Calibrated AI/AN-only model",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2024$FMD, calibrated_2024, aian_2024$RAW_WEIGHT))
), fill = TRUE)
save_table(calibration_audit, "19_aian_only_2024_calibration")
print(calibration_audit)
```

## 6. Compare both frozen models on the *same* 2025 AI/AN respondents

The 2025 input is the previously saved Notebook 07 scored checkpoint, preserving the exact 2025 sample and the national model's frozen predictions. 

Comparing survey-weighted **AUROC**, **Brier score**, **mean predicted probability**, and **calibration error**. The prevalence-only reference uses the *AI/AN training prevalence from 2014–2022*.

```{r paired-2025-aian-evaluation}
# Predict only the AI/AN respondents from the already prepared 2025 checkpoint.
aian_raw_2025 <- predict_classifier(aian_model, aian_2025)
aian_prob_2025 <- calibrate_probabilities(
    aian_raw_2025,
    aian_calibrator$intercept,
    aian_calibrator$slope
)
national_prob_2025 <- as.numeric(aian_2025$selected_probability)
if (any(!is.finite(aian_prob_2025)) ||
    any(aian_prob_2025 < 0 | aian_prob_2025 > 1)) {
    stop("New 2025 model returned an invalid probability.")
}

# Both models are evaluated on the same source_row_id, outcome, and survey weight.
comparison_2025 <- data.table::rbindlist(list(
    data.frame(model = "National logistic (frozen)",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2025$FMD, national_prob_2025, aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT)),
    data.frame(model = "AI/AN-only logistic (new)",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2025$FMD, aian_prob_2025, aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT)),
    data.frame(model = "AI/AN historical prevalence only",
               weighted_metrics(aian_2025$FMD,
                                rep(ai_training_prevalence, nrow(aian_2025)),
                                aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT))
), fill = TRUE)
save_table(comparison_2025, "19_aian_only_vs_national_2025_metrics")
print(comparison_2025)

# The comparison is descriptive. A paired survey-design bootstrap would be
# required to quantify uncertainty around the difference in model performance.
new_metrics <- comparison_2025[model == "AI/AN-only logistic (new)"]
national_metrics <- comparison_2025[model == "National logistic (frozen)"]
difference <- data.table::data.table(
    comparison = "AI/AN-only minus frozen national (on AI/AN 2025)",
    auc_difference = new_metrics$auc - national_metrics$auc,
    brier_difference = new_metrics$brier - national_metrics$brier,
    calibration_error_difference = new_metrics$calibration_error -
                                   national_metrics$calibration_error
)
save_table(difference, "19_aian_only_vs_national_2025_differences")
print(difference)

# Save a respondent-level comparison
scored_comparison <- data.table::data.table(
    source_row_id = aian_2025$source_row_id,
    YEAR = aian_2025$YEAR,
    cohort = aian_2025$cohort,
    FMD = aian_2025$FMD,
    STRAT = aian_2025$STRAT,
    PSU = aian_2025$PSU,
    RAW_WEIGHT = aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT,

)
save_once_rds(scored_comparison, "checkpoints", "19_aian_only_paired_2025")


```

## 7. Explore classification thresholds for each model

A confusion matrix depends on a selected probability cutoff. We compare the fixed illustrative thresholds **0.16, 0.20, and 0.50** and report sensitivity, specificity, precision, and fraction flagged. These thresholds are not recommended screening cutoffs.

```{r paired-2025-classification-thresholds}
safe_fraction19 <- function(n, d) if (is.finite(d) && d > 0) n / d else NA_real_

weighted_threshold_metrics19 <- function(y, probability, weight, cutoff, model_name) {
    positive <- probability >= cutoff
    tp <- sum(weight[y == 1 & positive])
    fn <- sum(weight[y == 1 & !positive])
    fp <- sum(weight[y == 0 & positive])
    tn <- sum(weight[y == 0 & !positive])
    data.table::data.table(
        model = model_name,
        threshold = cutoff,
        respondents = length(y),
        observed_fmd_n = sum(y == 1),
        flagged_n = sum(positive),
        observed_prevalence = safe_fraction19(tp + fn, tp + fn + fp + tn),
        fraction_flagged = safe_fraction19(tp + fp, tp + fn + fp + tn),
        sensitivity = safe_fraction19(tp, tp + fn),
        specificity = safe_fraction19(tn, tn + fp),
        precision_ppv = safe_fraction19(tp, tp + fp),
        accuracy = safe_fraction19(tp + tn, tp + fn + fp + tn),
        balanced_accuracy = (safe_fraction19(tp, tp + fn) +
                             safe_fraction19(tn, tn + fp)) / 2,
        f1 = safe_fraction19(2 * tp, 2 * tp + fp + fn)
    )
}

thresholds <- c(0.16, 0.20, 0.50)
threshold_rows <- list()
row_ix <- 0L
for (cutoff in thresholds) {
    for (model_name in c("National logistic (frozen)", "AI/AN-only logistic (new)")) {
        row_ix <- row_ix + 1L
        p <- if (model_name == "National logistic (frozen)") {
            national_prob_2025
        } else {
            aian_prob_2025
        }
        threshold_rows[[row_ix]] <- weighted_threshold_metrics19(
            aian_2025$FMD, p, aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT, cutoff, model_name
        )
    }
}
threshold_audit <- data.table::rbindlist(threshold_rows)
save_table(threshold_audit, "19_aian_only_2025_threshold_metrics")
print(threshold_audit)
```

```{r roc-auc-and-confusion-matrices}

# ============================================================
# 19 — ROC / AUROC AND CONFUSION MATRICES
# 2025 AI/AN-alone respondents
# ============================================================

# Uses objects already created in Notebook 19:
#   aian_2025
#   national_prob_2025
#   aian_prob_2025
#
# No model retraining is required.

y <- as.integer(aian_2025$FMD)
w <- as.numeric(aian_2025$RAW_WEIGHT)

model_predictions <- list(
    "National logistic" = national_prob_2025,
    "AI/AN-only logistic" = aian_prob_2025
)

stopifnot(
    all(y %in% c(0L, 1L)),
    all(is.finite(w) & w > 0),
    all(vapply(
        model_predictions,
        function(p) length(p) == length(y) &&
            all(is.finite(p) & p >= 0 & p <= 1),
        logical(1)
    ))
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Calculate survey-weighted ROC coordinates and AUROC
# ------------------------------------------------------------

weighted_roc <- function(y, probability, weight) {

    d <- data.table::data.table(
        score = as.numeric(probability),
        outcome = y,
        weight = weight
    )

    # Group tied probability scores together.
    d <- d[
        ,
        .(
            positive_weight = sum(weight[outcome == 1L]),
            negative_weight = sum(weight[outcome == 0L])
        ),
        by = score
    ]

    data.table::setorder(d, -score)

    total_positive <- sum(d$positive_weight)
    total_negative <- sum(d$negative_weight)

    if (total_positive <= 0 || total_negative <= 0) {
        stop("ROC requires both outcome classes.")
    }

    roc <- data.table::data.table(
        FPR = c(0, cumsum(d$negative_weight) / total_negative),
        TPR = c(0, cumsum(d$positive_weight) / total_positive)
    )

    auc <- sum(
        diff(roc$FPR) *
        (
            head(roc$TPR, -1) +
            tail(roc$TPR, -1)
        ) / 2
    )

    list(roc = roc, auc = auc)
}

roc_results <- lapply(
    model_predictions,
    function(p) weighted_roc(y, p, w)
)

auc_table <- data.table::rbindlist(
    lapply(names(roc_results), function(name) {
        data.table::data.table(
            model = name,
            AUROC = roc_results[[name]]$auc
        )
    })
)

print(auc_table)
save_table(auc_table, "19_2025_aian_roc_auc_comparison")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Plot ROC curves
# ------------------------------------------------------------

roc_data <- data.table::rbindlist(
    lapply(names(roc_results), function(name) {

        d <- data.table::copy(roc_results[[name]]$roc)

        d[
            ,
            model := paste0(
                name,
                " (AUROC = ",
                sprintf("%.3f", roc_results[[name]]$auc),
                ")"
            )
        ]

        d
    })
)

roc_colors <- stats::setNames(
    c(
        atg_palette[["rust"]],
        atg_palette[["gold"]]
    ),
    unique(roc_data$model)
)

p_roc <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    roc_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = FPR,
        y = TPR,
        color = model
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(
        intercept = 0,
        slope = 1,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = "gray65"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_step(linewidth = 1.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = roc_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 AI/AN model comparison: ROC curves",
        subtitle = "Survey-weighted ROC | Same AI/AN respondents",
        x = "False positive rate (1 - specificity)",
        y = "True positive rate (sensitivity)",
        color = "Model"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )

show_and_save(
    p_roc,
    "19_2025_aian_roc_curves",
    9,
    7
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate weighted confusion matrices
# ------------------------------------------------------------

thresholds <- c(0.16, 0.20, 0.50)

cm_rows <- list()
row_index <- 0L

for (cutoff in thresholds) {

    for (model_name in names(model_predictions)) {

        predicted <- as.integer(
            model_predictions[[model_name]] >= cutoff
        )

        for (actual_value in c(1L, 0L)) {

            for (predicted_value in c(0L, 1L)) {

                row_index <- row_index + 1L

                selected <- (
                    y == actual_value &
                    predicted == predicted_value
                )

                cm_rows[[row_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
                    model = model_name,
                    threshold = cutoff,
                    actual = actual_value,
                    predicted = predicted_value,
                    respondent_n = sum(selected),
                    weighted_n = sum(w[selected])
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

cm <- data.table::rbindlist(cm_rows)

# Percentages within each actual outcome group.
cm[
    ,
    weighted_percent :=
        100 * weighted_n / sum(weighted_n),
    by = .(model, threshold, actual)
]

cm[
    ,
    actual_label := factor(
        ifelse(actual == 1L, "Actual FMD", "Actual no FMD"),
        levels = c("Actual no FMD", "Actual FMD")
    )
]

cm[
    ,
    predicted_label := factor(
        ifelse(predicted == 1L, "Predicted FMD", "Predicted no FMD"),
        levels = c("Predicted no FMD", "Predicted FMD")
    )
]

cm[
    ,
    cell_type := ifelse(
        actual == predicted,
        ifelse(actual == 1L, "True positive", "True negative"),
        ifelse(actual == 1L, "False negative", "False positive")
    )
]

print(cm)

save_table(
    cm,
    "19_2025_aian_confusion_matrices"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Visualize confusion matrices at each threshold
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cm_colors <- c(
    "True positive" = "#6BB5AE",
    "True negative" = "#D4E4E0",
    "False positive" = "#F1D5A2",
    "False negative" = "#E5B1A0"
)

for (cutoff in thresholds) {

    plot_data <- cm[threshold == cutoff]

    p_cm <- ggplot2::ggplot(
        plot_data,
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = predicted_label,
            y = actual_label,
            fill = cell_type
        )
    ) +
        ggplot2::geom_tile(
            color = "white",
            linewidth = 2
        ) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
            ggplot2::aes(
                label = sprintf(
                    "%.1f%%\nn = %s",
                    weighted_percent,
                    format(
                        respondent_n,
                        big.mark = ",",
                        scientific = FALSE
                    )
                )
            ),
            size = 4.5,
            color = "#3F3027",
            lineheight = 1.5
        ) +
        ggplot2::facet_wrap(
            ~model,
            nrow = 1
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
            values = cm_colors
        ) +
        ggplot2::coord_equal() +
        atg_theme() +
        ggplot2::theme(
            axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
                angle = 0,
                hjust = 0.5
            ),
            legend.position = "bottom",
            panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()
        ) +
        ggplot2::labs(
            title = paste0(
                "2025 AI/AN confusion matrices: cutoff ",
                sprintf("%.2f", cutoff)
            ),
            subtitle = paste(
                "Survey-weighted row percentages;",
                "unweighted respondent counts"
            ),
            x = "Model classification",
            y = "Reported outcome",
            fill = "Classification"
        )

    show_and_save(
        p_cm,
        paste0(
            "19_2025_aian_confusion_cutoff_",
            sprintf("%02d", round(cutoff * 100))
        ),
        11,
        6
    )
}

cat("\n[COMPLETE] ROC curves and confusion matrices saved.\n")

```
